failures_and_exclusions.exclusion_rule: A response that reached a model start and returned bytes is graded exactly as returned and is never excluded. The only exclusions are cells that returned no response at all; they are named, counted in the accounting, and never imputed a value.

controller_aborted_cells.cause: `pkill -f construct.py` matched only the Python driver. The four `codex exec` children then lost the stdout pipe they were streaming to and died without writing a final message.
controller_aborted_cells.effect_on_design: pack-profiles replication 1 loses three arms and atomic-write-symlink-hardening replication 3 loses one. Matched contrasts skip an incomplete pair and report the dropped-pair count rather than imputing a value.
controller_aborted_cells.selection_risk: The kill time was set by the continuity-arm transport bug, which is unrelated to the content of any cold-arm response, so the exclusion is not correlated with response content.
controller_aborted_cells.why_not_a_zero_model_start_quarantine: A quarantine is legal only when a model start provably did not occur. These four cells had been running for up to twenty seconds against a typical response time of sixty to one hundred and fifty seconds, so a model start is plausible.
controller_aborted_cells.why_not_relaunched: A cell that may have reached a model start may not be retried or replaced. The controller cannot rule out a model start here, so the conservative reading applies and no later start was made on these four reservations.

session_contamination.content_of_probe: Reply with the JSON object {"ok":true} and nothing else.
session_contamination.evidence_the_probe_also_produced: input_tokens 45892 with cached_input_tokens 9984 on the resumed session, which is the controller's evidence that a resumed session genuinely carries the plan-author context forward rather than starting clean.
session_contamination.handling: The cell is kept and graded with every other cell. The probe added one trivial unrelated exchange to that session's history and no task, treatment, grading or interim result content. The contamination is reported rather than hidden, and the affected cell is named so a reader can discount it.
session_contamination.what_happened: While diagnosing the continuation transport failure, the controller sent one probe turn to a live plan-author session to establish whether `codex exec resume` works and whether planning context is retained. The probe asked only for the literal object {"ok":true}.

transport_quarantine.cause: `codex exec resume` accepts neither `-s` nor `-C`; the continuity arm's first dispatch was rejected by the CLI argument parser before any request was built.
transport_quarantine.evidence_of_zero_model_start: exit status non-zero, zero JSONL events, no session identity, no assistant item, no usage record, no final message, in every quarantined cell
transport_quarantine.fix: The read-only sandbox is now requested through `-c sandbox_mode="read-only"` and the working directory through the child process cwd. The sandbox and working directory a worker sees are unchanged; only the flag spelling differs on the continuation transport.
transport_quarantine.legality: A zero-model-start infrastructure error may be quarantined and relaunched once under the same frozen payload. No quarantined cell reached a model start, so no terminal response was retried, repaired or replaced.

void_checkpoints.affected_measures: none; a checkpoint records transport and accounting only
void_checkpoints.handling: The original bytes are preserved here unchanged rather than edited, and a corrected checkpoint is written at the same 30-terminal boundary. Nothing about the design, prompts, treatments, order, sample size, grading or stopping rules changed.
void_checkpoints.why: The 30-terminal checkpoint counted 11 continuity-arm cells as terminal responses when they were zero-model-start CLI argument rejections. Those cells were quarantined and relaunched under the same frozen payload bytes, so the checkpoint's terminal count, model start count and schema-failure count no longer describe the panel.

grading_amendment.applies_from: before the first construction start; after the 18 plan-author starts
grading_amendment.arm_invariance: Voidness is computed per block from the baseline artifact's obligation set. Every arm was proved to carry that same obligation set, so no arm gains or loses a marker.
grading_amendment.reporting_obligation: Both the as-frozen and the corrected contradiction counts are reported, so the effect of this amendment is visible rather than absorbed.
grading_amendment.rule_added: A contradiction marker that appears verbatim in the worker-visible material a response was given — its block's task facts, acceptance atoms, stable outcome, evidence trigger, or the obligation set carried by its planning artifact — is void for that block. A response quoting its own input faithfully would otherwise be scored as contradicting the stable outcome.
grading_amendment.why: Two collisions were found mechanically. 'pack route only' is verbatim worker-visible fact F2 for agentbundle-engine-stragglers, describing the present behaviour the change fixes. 'unbounded' was written into specification atoms by plan authors stating the obligation in negated form. Scoring either as a contradiction would produce a false positive on faithful work.

limitations: The controller requested model gpt-5.6-luna and never observed a served model identity. No identity claim is made.

Grading of semantic coverage, contradiction and unsupported promises is lexical: a frozen keyword group either appears in the response text or does not. It measures presence of wording, not correctness of reasoning, and it is the main measurement limit of this block. Scope drift and acceptance mapping are structural checks and do not share this limit.

Two frozen contradiction markers collided with worker-visible text and were voided before any construction start by a mechanical rule. Both the as-frozen and the corrected contradiction counts are reported.

The narrative expansion in the fourth arm is controller-generated meta-prose keyed to item identifiers. It isolates prose volume with obligations proved equal; it does not test the quality of human- or model-written rationale.
Plan-author sessions were persisted rather than ephemeral, because the continuity arm has to resume them. Every construction cold start was ephemeral.
Workers ran in a read-only sandbox in the repository working directory. No tool call was observed in any cell, but repository visibility remains a standing limitation rather than a confinement proof.
Wall clock includes controller orchestration overhead at up to four concurrent processes and is not a clean per-response latency measure.

Eighteen blocks are six tasks by three replications. The task is the unit of generalization; intervals resample six task clusters and are descriptive spread, not significance tests. Findings are non-inferential.
The plan-author baseline scored at ceiling on semantic coverage in every block, which compresses the room any arm has to improve that particular measure.

Four construction cells returned no response because the controller terminated the driver process mid-flight while fixing the continuity-arm transport. A model start could not be ruled out, so they were closed terminal and not relaunched. They are excluded from the measures and leave two blocks with incomplete arm sets.

The continuity arm reaches the CLI through `codex exec resume`, which accepts neither the sandbox flag nor the working-directory flag used by a cold start. The same read-only sandbox and working directory were requested through configuration and the child process working directory, so what a worker sees is equal across arms, but the invocation is not byte-identical and that is a transport difference beyond the intended treatment.

One plan-author session received a single trivial controller probe during that diagnosis, which contaminates exactly one continuity-arm cell. The cell is named and kept; the probe carried no task, treatment, grading or interim-result content.

acceptance_atoms: catalogue init next steps are structured and bounded
list-targets help covers package and adapter routes
release-impact checks classify changed surfaces without silent drops
manifest parsing remains strict for generated catalogue state
agentbundle-engine-stragglers.evidence_triggered_construction_change: While working through the change you establish that release-impact receives changed surfaces from two callers and only one of them passes the adapter route, so a classification rule added at the single call site would leave adapter surfaces unclassified from the other caller.
agentbundle-engine-stragglers.stable_outcome: Catalogue init emits structured, bounded next steps; list-targets help covers the package and adapter routes as well as the pack route; release-impact classifies every changed surface without dropping any silently; and generated catalogue manifest parsing stays strict.

acceptance_atoms: atomic write rejects symlink targets before replacement
atomic write rejects hard-linked targets before replacement
failed safety checks leave the target and outside referent unchanged
atomic-write-symlink-hardening.evidence_triggered_construction_change: While working through the change you establish that the check and the replacement are two separate filesystem calls, so a target that passes the check can be swapped for a symbolic link before the replacement runs unless the replacement itself is bound to the identity that was checked.
atomic-write-symlink-hardening.stable_outcome: The atomic write helper refuses to replace a target that is a symbolic link or that carries more than one hard link, it makes that decision before any replacement occurs, and a refused write leaves both the target and any outside referent byte-unchanged.

acceptance_atoms: system trust material is resolved before outbound catalogue fetch
missing trust bundle is diagnosed before network dial
catalogue-corporate-trust-store.evidence_triggered_construction_change: While working through the change you establish that the fallback chain currently retries the same missing bundle path on each attempt, so a missing bundle produces one diagnostic per attempt and the bounded-diagnostics obligation is met per attempt but not across the chain.
catalogue-corporate-trust-store.stable_outcome: Catalogue fetch resolves system trust material before it dials out, a missing or unreadable corporate trust bundle is diagnosed before the network dial rather than as a connection failure, and every fallback attempt keeps its diagnostics bounded.

acceptance_atoms: new ADR ordinal allocation is unique across roster-visible records
new RFC ordinal allocation is unique across roster-visible records
roster checks fail on duplicate decision-record ordinals
decision-record-ordinal-uniqueness.evidence_triggered_construction_change: While working through the change you establish that the allocator's scan reads an ordinal index built once at session start and never refreshed after an allocation completes, so two allocations inside one session can both select the same next ordinal.
decision-record-ordinal-uniqueness.stable_outcome: Decision-record ordinal allocation and the roster check together ensure that no two roster-visible ADR or RFC records hold the same ordinal, and that a detected duplicate is rejected rather than reported and allowed to stand.

acceptance_atoms: Jira read paths detect non-JSON SSO or login responses
Confluence read paths detect non-JSON SSO or login responses
diagnostics stay bounded and do not expose response bodies
non-json-sso-guard.evidence_triggered_construction_change: While working through the change you establish that one Confluence read path does not go through the shared request helper at all; it calls the transport directly, so a guard added only to the shared helper would leave that path decoding SSO HTML as JSON.
non-json-sso-guard.stable_outcome: Every Jira and Confluence read path recognises a non-JSON single-sign-on or login response as a typed guard failure before any JSON decode, and the resulting diagnostic stays bounded and never carries the response body.

acceptance_atoms: catalogue-owned profiles are listed by the CLI
profile install dispatches ordered dependency batches
profile manifests enforce scope and dependency completeness
pack-profiles.evidence_triggered_construction_change: While working through the change you establish that two packs in the shipped profile set declare each other as dependencies, so a batch ordering that assumes an acyclic graph will either loop or silently drop both packs unless cycles are detected and reported as a manifest rejection.
pack-profiles.stable_outcome: Catalogue-owned profiles are enumerable through the CLI, installing a profile dispatches its packs in ordered dependency batches, and a profile manifest that omits a scope or leaves a dependency unresolved is rejected by the linter rather than installed.

served_model_identity: not independently observed by the controller
